name: TN-04
label: Likely R

key_factors: Incumbent DesJarlais running with large financial edge
Democratic challenger underfunded with minimal cash
model.rationale: The R+11 lean, DesJarlais's incumbency and roughly nine-to-one fundraising advantage, and Polymarket pricing the Republican at 94% all point to a comfortable Republican hold. With no polls or expert ratings available, the forecast stays close to fundamentals.
model.watch: A surge of outside spending against DesJarlais, whose past personal controversies could resurface, is the main path to a closer race.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Republican Scott DesJarlais seeks another term in a Middle Tennessee district that leans about eleven points Republican. He enters the general election with a large financial advantage, roughly half a million dollars on hand, while Democrat Victoria Broderick has raised under $60,000 and has little cash remaining. Two independents are also on the ballot but lack significant resources.

No public polls or expert ratings cover this race, so the outlook rests on district fundamentals and money. Prediction markets give the Republican about a 94% chance of holding the seat. The district's lean and the incumbent's advantages make a Democratic upset possible but unlikely, with a Republican win of roughly fifteen points the central expectation.
